$comment: A correct route whose reason is written the way a person writes, rather than as a list of the tokens the
fixture names. It is here because the constructed answers the contract oracles are checked against build their
reason out of the fixture's own tokens, which proves an oracle can resolve and proves nothing about whether a
real sentence clears it. This one is that sentence.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus, of the menu it is scored against, and of the user's message.
Those three plus the reply are the whole input to scoreCase, so all three are stored here rather than read
live: a replay has to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: The tests exist and the judgment asked for is about how they are written, not about what they cover. The message says badly written, and that is the word a grounded reason repeats.
